label: late original-phase / <DEL> steps of long sequences, gated by early-token content (first token in {x,z,c,0,1,o,e,n})
explanation: Fires only at steps t=4..9 of the original phase and at the <DEL> step, never in the copy phase and never at t<4. Within that window it is restricted to long sequences (L>=7 holds ~98% of mass, mostly L=8-9) and rate grows with orig_idx (15% at orig_idx 8). (phase<=1)&(t>=6) covers 96% of activation mass but only 7% precision, so which sequences fire depends on content: lift is ~3x when the first original token is one of x,z,c,0,1,o,e,n (early tokens matter most; requiring both orig(0) and orig(1) in that set gives precision 0.43), and the current input is <DEL> (31% of mass) or one of b,p,s,i,3,j,v,u (b/p/s ~3x lift). Mostly on first occurrences of the input token (in_first, 91% of mass). Peak activations are on the last original token or the one before it, with smaller values on <DEL>. This looks like a distributed readout of the hidden state accumulated from early tokens rather than a clean single-token rule; the content gating is only approximated by the token sets. Magnitude claims beyond the position/token trends were not checked.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: x, z, c, 0, 1, o; least: s, b, j, p) and the current input token, by phase (input phase: b, p, s, 3; delimiter step: <DEL>; copy phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: t=7, t=8, L=9 & t=8.
